question: On boards with differential pairs (named by KRT's suffix rules), does the krt-diffpair stage with coupled via pairs, intra-pair skew compensation and the optimizer exclusion (run before the fanout, pairs inferred from net names) keep at least 90 % of each board's pair copper within ±10 % of the gap, without a new clearance violation, a via in a pad, or a single-ended net left unrouted that the run without the stage routes?

off.engine: freerouting-rs at the commit that lands X09, freerouting-krt's in-process harness (the CLI does not call freerouting_krt::register yet, C07)
off.command: X09_SET=tools/bench/sets/x09-pairs.txt X09_RECORDS=<out>/records.json cargo test --release -p freerouting-krt --test diffpair_vias measurement_records_on_a_set -- --ignored --exact --nocapture

settings.all other settings: the defaults (optimizer on, as the CLI)

on.engine: the same commit and harness; a full route with the stage selected
on.command: the same run; one records file holds both arms

boards.dsn: three synthetic boards in crates/freerouting-krt/tests/data and the three boards of F03.3's out-of-repo corpus that X08 registered (target/corpus/prepped, tools/corpus/prep.sh)

eligibility: decided from the inputs: a board with at least one pair by KRT's naming rules whose two nets have two pins each. A row whose pairs the stage skips (more than two pins) or reports as crossing is neutral and printed.
grading: Rust's DRC (DesignRulesChecker: clearance violations, incompletes per net) and the via-in-pad test of crates/freerouting-krt/tests/diffpair_vias.rs on both arms; the coupling of each pair from freerouting_krt::diffpair::report::coupling_on over its layers on the final board. drc_real (KiCad grading, F02.6) of the corpus rows' sessions is a second step once the harness writes their SES and C07 registers the stage in the CLI; until then clearance_violations stands in for it (not graded is never a pass).

metric_definitions.via_in_pad: vias whose centre lies in a pin's pad on a shared layer
metric_definitions.unrouted_single_ended: the sum of DesignRulesChecker::incomplete_count_of over every net that is not in a name-inferred pair
metric_definitions.coupled_share: over the name-inferred pairs of two-pin nets: the summed length of their copper within ±10 % of the gap of the partner's copper divided by their summed copper length (report::coupling_on over the pair's start and end layers)
metric_definitions.pairs_coupled: those pairs with a coupling share of at least 0.9

pass_rule.per_board: on arm: coupled_share >= 0.90, via_in_pad = 0, clearance_violations <= off, unrouted_single_ended <= off

decision_table.pass: the stage may become a default-on candidate; the default changes only after KiCad grading (F02.6) of the corpus rows and the orchestrator's decision, with a DIVERGENCES.md line if it does
decision_table.fail: the stage stays selectable and off by default, and the numbers are recorded in X09.5; a guard regression is a bug to fix first

timing: the registered run waits for P04's default-tree decision (P00 README 'Order'): both arms route, so their numbers depend on the tree. A pre-P04 smoke of the synthetic rows is recorded in X09.5, not as the result.
